On [0,1), let a = floor(n*frac(x)); then the value at frac(x) is bounded above by the endpoint value a/n. Rewrite that endpoint value as a weighted sum of least residues of k*a modulo n. Rearrangement shows the weighted sum is maximized when the residues are sorted in nonincreasing order, and the gcd-based residue lemma gives the pointwise bound needed to reach H_n-1. Conversely, every x with fractional part in that interval gives floor(kx)=k-1 for all 1<=k<=n, so the expression evaluates to H_n-1. Therefore the maximal value is H_n-1 and the maximizers are exactly the real x whose fractional part lies in [(n-1)/n,1).
